title: Nvidia vs. Alphabet: What Revenue Trends Reveal About the AI Leaders
excerpt: NVIDIA and Alphabet both rode the AI wave to blockbuster quarters, but their financials tell two stories so different they raise a harder question: which bus...
content_html:
Quick Read

  • NVDA posted 85% revenue growth to $82B while GOOG grew 24% to $120B, exposing two distinct AI business models from the same tailwind.

  • Alphabet suspended buybacks, doubled long-term debt to $98B, and guided $180-190B in capex, driving free cash flow negative at -$5.86B.

  • NVIDIA's 75% gross margins and 41x P/E look defensible against 85% growth; Alphabet at 15x P/E offers ad cash flows as a capex-fatigue cushion.

  • Don't wait: the analyst who called NVIDIA in 2010 just revealed his top 10 AI stocks. See the full list FREE now.

NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) and Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG) both reported quarters that reshape how investors should think about AI leadership.

NVIDIA delivered $81.615 billion in revenue, up 85.23%. Alphabet pulled in $119.80 billion, up 24.2%. Same tailwind, very different business models, and the results expose the split.

Data Center Explodes for NVIDIA. Cloud Accelerates for Alphabet.

NVIDIA's Data Center segment hit $75.25 billion, up 92%, with networking alone growing 199% on InfiniBand, NVLink, and Spectrum-X demand.

Jensen Huang framed it plainly: "The buildout of AI factories, the largest infrastructure expansion in human history, is accelerating at extraordinary speed." Guidance for Q2 lands at $91 billion, and notably excludes any China Data Center compute revenue.

Alphabet's headline was Google Cloud reaching $24.77 billion, growing 82%. Sundar Pichai emphasized adoption: "Nearly 90% of the Fortune 100 using it" referring to Gemini Enterprise, while Gemini models process 22 billion API tokens per minute. Search advertising still funds the whole machine at $63.27 billion, up 17%.

Picks and Shovels vs. Full Vertical Stack

NVIDIA sells the compute. Alphabet builds on it, and also buys it. Pichai even said Google Cloud will be "among the first to offer NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72", which makes GOOG both a customer and a competitor thanks to its own TPUs. That vertical integration is the pitch: "We're unique in the market because of our vertically optimized AI stack."

NVIDIA hiked its dividend from $0.01 to $0.25 and authorized $80 billion in buybacks. Alphabet went the other direction, suspending buybacks and raising roughly $70 billion in debt and equity to fund a capex plan now guided to $180-190 billion for 2026. Free cash flow at GOOG turned negative at -$5.86 billion. That is the cost of racing to own the stack.

NVIDIA（纳斯达克股票代码：NVDA）和 Alphabet（纳斯达克股票代码：GOOG）均公布了重塑投资者对人工智能领导地位的看法的季度报告。

NVIDIA 营收 816.15 亿美元，同比增长 85.23%。 Alphabet 的收入为 1198 亿美元，增长 24.2%。 同样的顺风车，截然不同的商业模式，结果暴露了分歧。

NVIDIA 数据中心呈爆炸式增长。 云为 Alphabet 加速。

NVIDIA 的数据中心业务收入达到 752.5 亿美元，增长 92%，仅网络业务就因 InfiniBand、NVLink 和 Spectrum-X 需求增长了 199%。

黄仁勋明确表示：“人工智能工厂的建设是人类历史上最大规模的基础设施扩张，正在以惊人的速度加速。” 第二季度指导值为 910 亿美元，特别不包括任何中国数据中心计算收入。

Alphabet 的头条新闻是 Google Cloud 营收达到 247.7 亿美元，增长 82%。 Sundar Pichai 强调了采用率：“财富 100 强中近 90% 的企业都在使用它”，指的是 Gemini Enterprise，而 Gemini 模型每分钟处理 220 亿个 API 令牌。 搜索广告仍为整机提供资金632.7亿美元，增长17%。

镐和铲子与全垂直堆叠

NVIDIA 出售计算设备。 Alphabet 以此为基础，也收购了它。 Pichai 甚至表示，Google Cloud 将成为“首批提供 NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 的公司之一”，这使得 GOOG 凭借自己的 TPU 既成为客户，又成为竞争对手。 垂直整合就是这样的基调：“我们在市场上是独一无二的，因为我们有垂直优化的人工智能堆栈。”
